entities.text:
Ashok Shukla (Sharma) Vs. State of M.P.)
Gwalior
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Shri Mukesh Sharma, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Vivek Bhargava, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State.
With consent heard finally.

This is the first bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. preferred by the applicant for the alleged offences registered at Crime No.174/2018 at Police Station Dimni, District Morena,
punishable under Sections 269, 272, 420 of the IPC and Sections 55, 56, 57, 59 & 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
Applicant is apprehending his arrest on the basis of false/ alleged case registered against him.
Except Section 420 of the IPC, other offences are bailable in nature and ingredients of Section 420 of IPC are not available in the present case.
Prosecution has not followed the procedure as prescribed under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
The Food Safety Officer ought to have filed private complaint as per provisions contained in Section 420 of IPC.
Therefore, he be given the benefit of anticipatory bail.

Learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and submits on the basis of case diary that the case is serious in nature because applicant was involved in preparation of milk,
milk products from urea and other chemicals.
Offence is against the society.
Sample has been taken and referred in the sealed cover.
Such milk products and Ghee causing serious health hazard to the public at large.
Investigation would unfold the exact nature of offence and there is likelihood that additional offences may also be added in the case in hand.

If anticipatory bail is THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Ashok Shukla (Sharma) Vs. State of M.P.) granted to the applicant then applicant shall not cooperate in the investigation and would indulge in the same nature of offence again.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Ashok Shukla (Sharma) Vs. State of M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Perusal of case diary, FIR, Panchnama and the statement of Food Safety Officer, it appears that offences of the applicant is against the society at large and against very human existence, wherein urea and other chemicals are used for preparation of milk, milk products and Ghee.
At this juncture no case is made out for grant of anticipatory bail.
Therefore, it is hereby dismissed.
